rule: picks use nothing after the Friday before the Monday; scored Monday open to Friday close

why.XOM: XLE's largest holding (22%) has finally joined the breakout, up 4.09% to $165.99 with RSI only 51 and 3% below its 52-week high, so it has the most room of the leaders while WTI holds $100 with Hormuz constrained, Bab el-Mandeb threatened and no OPEC+ meeting until Oct 4.
why.COP: The largest pure oil producer on the sheet closed at a fresh 52-week high ($137.35), yet producer stocks still lag $100 crude, so it can re-rate on a one-and-done hike or a worse supply shock, with the average analyst target about 6% above the price.
why.VLO: The sector's strongest trend (+66% in 12 weeks, fresh 52-week-high close) is backed by record diesel refining margins above $100 a barrel and ~97% utilization, which the Houthi push on Bab el-Mandeb can only tighten; I take it despite an overbought RSI of 80.
why.AMD: It is the high-beta way to play faster AI demand: its Helios rack system began shipping and management put its 2030 market at $2T, driving an 8.07% rally on that news while the chip ETF (SMH) was flat, and it would lead XLK through $188.74 if Wednesday's hike is framed as insurance.
why.LLY: It is the biggest lever on the healthcare bounce: at about 12% of XLV it sits at an RSI of 2.5, about 5% above its 200-day ($1,062), after selling driven by higher rates and a knock-on from a rival's failed heart-drug trial rather than any damage to its obesity-drug sales, so a one-and-done Fed should lift it first.

why.GOOGL: The synthesis calls it the 'cleanest megacap value in the sector': it trades at 17.6x trailing earnings with net cash, the benign Brinkema opinion removed the divestiture tail, it closed above its ~$345.58 50-day line, and neither the Oct 2 final judgment nor the Oct 28 print falls this week.
why.PGR: At 11.3x with EPS still up 10.1%, it is the cheapest sound financial on the table and the purest form of 'own the float, not the loan book': a short-duration portfolio that reinvests at higher yields in a hiking cycle, with no credit-cycle or oil exposure.
why.GS: At 14.5x trailing (~11x forward, ~21% to target) with EPS up 43.9% after five straight down days, this is my 'best entry of the year if the credit fear is phantom', and live spreads (HY OAS 270, IG 78 and tightening through a hike) say it may be.
why.LNG: At 15.4x trailing, Cheniere is investment-grade and sells mostly under long-term contracts, so it earns shortage economics from a Hormuz squeeze (four transits Thursday) without needing either disputed WTI print to be right.
why.REGN: The cheapest healthcare name on the table at 16.7x, with a large net-cash balance sheet, in the one defensive sector that actually defended (XLV +1.83%, 50-day reclaimed), and it does not report until Oct 28.

Cecil.summary: This book buys cheap, real earnings that don't depend on the discount rate or on which oil price is right: net-cash GOOGL and REGN, float-funded PGR, contracted LNG, plus GS as the one contrarian bet that live credit spreads are right and the bank selloff is wrong. I passed on the rate-sensitive income names (O, VICI, the utilities) because a 5Y or 7Y auction tail into $192B of supply could push the 10Y through 5.05%, kept PEP behind its GIS gate, and skipped cheap names with shrinking earnings (STZ, SM, CALM, HON) because cheap is not a catalyst. COST reports Thursday and was off-limits, and VLO at RSI 86.7, above its target, has already been harvested and is not cheap.
